audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph supporters joining David at Ziklag and Hebron, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for defectors and divided loyalties, Benjaminite kin of Saul, animalized warrior imagery, river crossing and valley flight, betrayal fears, spirit speech, Philistine rejection, raider conflict, troop census, command hierarchy, Issachar time-discernment, unity rhetoric, and food logistics.

verses.restored: These came to David at Ziklag while he was restrained from presence of Saul son of Kish; they were among mighty warriors, helpers in war.
They were armed with bows and could use right and left hands for stones and arrows; they were from Saul's relatives of Benjamin.
Chief Ahiezer, then Joash sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet sons of Azmaveth; Beracah and Jehu the Anathothite;
Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, mighty among thirty and over thirty; Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, Jozabad the Gederathite;
Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, Shephatiah the Haruphite;
Elkanah, Isshiah, Azarel, Joezer, Jashobeam the Korahites;
Joelah and Zebadiah sons of Jeroham from Gedor.
Some Gadites separated to David at wilderness stronghold, mighty warriors trained for battle, handling shield and spear; faces compared to lions and speed to gazelles on mountains.
Ezer first, Obadiah second, Eliab third,
Mishmannah fourth, Jeremiah fifth,
Attai sixth, Eliel seventh,
Johanan eighth, Elzabad ninth,
Jeremiah tenth, Machbannai eleventh.
These Gadites were commanders; least over a hundred and greatest over a thousand, in military hierarchy.
These crossed Jordan in first month when it overflowed banks and put to flight all in valleys east and west.
Some from Benjamin and Judah came to stronghold to David.
David went to meet them and said, If you come in peace to help me, my heart shall unite with you; if to betray me to enemies though no violence is in my hands, may Divine of ancestors see and judge.

Spirit clothed Amasai chief of thirty, and he said, Yours are we, David, and with you, son of Jesse. Peace, peace to you and peace to helpers, for your Divine helps you. David received them and made them commanders.

Some from Manasseh joined David when he came with Philistines for battle against Saul, but they did not help Philistines; their rulers sent him away after counsel, saying, At cost of our heads he may defect to Saul his master.
As he went to Ziklag, Manassites joined him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, commanders of thousands in Manasseh.
They helped David against raiding band, for all were mighty warriors and became commanders in army.
Day by day people came to help David until there was a great camp, like camp of Divine.
These are numbers of armed bands who came to David at Hebron to turn kingdom of Saul to him according to word of YHWH, in narrator's theology.
From Judah, bearing shield and spear: six thousand eight hundred armed for battle.
From Simeon, mighty warriors for battle: seven thousand one hundred.
From Levi: four thousand six hundred.
Jehoiada leader of Aaronites, with three thousand seven hundred;
Zadok, a young mighty warrior, and twenty-two commanders from ancestral house.
From Benjamin, Saul's relatives: three thousand, for until then most kept allegiance to house of Saul.
From Ephraim: twenty thousand eight hundred mighty warriors, renowned in ancestral houses.
From half-tribe Manasseh: eighteen thousand named to come make David king.
From Issachar, people understanding times and knowing what Israel should do: two hundred heads, and all relatives under their command.
From Zebulun: fifty thousand going out to battle, arraying with all weapons, keeping rank with undivided loyalty.
From Naphtali: one thousand commanders and thirty-seven thousand with shield and spear.
From Dan: twenty-eight thousand six hundred trained for battle.
From Asher: forty thousand going out for battle and trained for war.
From beyond Jordan—Reuben, Gad, half-Manasseh—with all battle weapons: one hundred twenty thousand.
All these warriors keeping rank came with whole heart to Hebron to make David king over all Israel; all rest of Israel were one heart to make David king, in idealized account.
They were there with David three days, eating and drinking, for relatives prepared for them.

Nearby people as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought bread on donkeys, camels, mules, oxen; food, flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance, for joy was in Israel.

translation_notes: People joining David are defectors, refugees, kin of Saul, military professionals, and political actors with complex loyalties; they are not a simple unanimous movement.
Lion-face and gazelle-speed comparisons are warrior poetry, not body ideals or permission to animalize people.
Verse 15's valley flight implies harm and displacement beyond the celebrated river crossing.
David's claim of innocent hands must be tested against 1 Samuel, including his raids and deception from Ziklag.
Amasai's spirit-inspired declaration does not make political allegiance infallible or criticism of David unfaithful.
The Philistine commanders' rejection of David reflects specific wartime risk and may not justify profiling refugees or dual-loyalty minorities.
Troop numbers and command structures reflect militarization, not the total value or consent of each tribe.
Understanding the times in verse 32 is political discernment in context, not a warrant for authoritarian astrologers or secret-knowledge elites.
Idealized one-heart unity can erase dissent, women, noncombatants, Saul loyalists, and coerced participation.
The final feast depends on transport workers, farmers, bakers, animal labor, and regional supply chains.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to glorify defection, militarism, ethnic profiling, leader cults, forced unanimity, or obedience to spiritual-political elites. Preserve divided loyalties, civilian impact, logistical labor, and the right to question David's claimed innocence.
